intent.raw_query: Eastern Europe city hop Prague + Budapest, $1200, 8 days, September 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Eastern Europe – Prague & Budapest

experiences.name: Prague Castle & St. Vitus Cathedral Exploration
experiences.description: Wander through the largest ancient castle complex in the world, exploring the stunning Gothic St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and the charming Golden Lane. Soak in panoramic views over Prague's red-roofed skyline and immerse yourself in over a thousand years of Bohemian history.

experiences.name: Old Town Square & Astronomical Clock Tour
experiences.description: Stroll through Prague's medieval Old Town Square, admire the iconic 15th-century Astronomical Clock (Orloj) as it chimes on the hour, and explore the Baroque and Gothic architecture surrounding the square. Stop at a local bakery for a warm trdelník pastry and absorb the vibrant street atmosphere.

experiences.name: Budapest Ruin Bar Crawl & Local Street Food Night
experiences.description: Dive into Budapest's legendary ruin bar scene starting at Szimpla Kert, the city's most famous bar built inside a crumbling Jewish Quarter building. Graze on local street food including lángos (deep-fried dough with sour cream and cheese), kürtőskalács, and chimney cake from nearby vendors while mingling with locals.

experiences.name: Thermal Bath Experience at Széchenyi Baths
experiences.description: Relax in one of Europe's largest and most spectacular thermal bath complexes, housed in a stunning Neo-Baroque palace in City Park. Soak in the outdoor and indoor pools fed by natural hot springs, a beloved Hungarian tradition dating back centuries. A perfect mid-trip recharge after days of city hopping.

experiences.name: Danube River Sunset Cruise with Hungarian Wine Tasting
experiences.description: Board a scenic evening cruise along the Danube River and witness Budapest's breathtaking illuminated skyline, including the Hungarian Parliament Building, Buda Castle, and the Chain Bridge. Enjoy a curated tasting of local Tokaj and Egri Bikavér wines while a guide shares stories of the city's rich history.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe – Prague & Budapest
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Eastern Europe – Prague & Budapest

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled – in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Václav Havel Airport Prague at 22:30. Clear customs, collect baggage, and take the affordable Airport Express bus (AE line) or night bus 910 to the city center. Check in to your accommodation, grab a late-night snack from a 24-hour convenience store or nearby kebab stand, and rest up for the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night snack from a 24-hour convenience store or street food stand near your accommodation (~€3–5)

day_by_day.notes: Keep your first night simple. Purchase a Prague public transport pass at the airport (3-day pass ~€10) to save money on buses, trams, and metro. Exchange a small amount of cash to Czech Koruna (CZK) at the airport for immediate needs, but avoid airport exchange booths for large amounts – use a local ATM in the city instead.

day_by_day.morning: Start your Prague adventure with a free self-guided walk across the iconic Charles Bridge (Karlův most) in the morning when crowds are thinner. Admire the 30 Baroque statues lining the bridge and enjoy panoramic views of the Vltava River. Continue into the Lesser Town (Malá Strana) and explore its charming cobblestone streets and colorful baroque architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head up to Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) – the largest ancient castle complex in the world. Walk the outer grounds and gardens for free, or purchase a budget Circuit B ticket (~€10) to enter St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and the Golden Lane. Spend 3–4 hours exploring the hilltop complex with sweeping views of the city below.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll down to the Old Town Square (Staroměstské náměstí) and watch the famous Astronomical Clock (Orloj) chime at the top of the hour. Browse the lively square, then head to a traditional Czech pub in the Old Town for a budget-friendly dinner. End the night with a cheap local Czech beer – Prague is famous for having some of the world's most affordable and best-quality lager.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh pastry (trdelník or rohlík) and coffee from a local bakery near your accommodation (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or a street food sausage (klobása) from an Old Town vendor (~€3–4)
meals.dinner: Traditional Czech goulash with bread dumplings at a local pub such as U Fleků or a similar budget pub (~€7–10 including a beer)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – Prague is very walkable but hilly near the castle. The castle grounds open at 06:00 and are best visited before 10:00 to beat tour groups. Free walking tours depart from Old Town Square daily at 10:00 and 14:00 – tip-based, great for budget travelers.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) – one of the best-preserved Jewish historic districts in Europe. Visit the exterior of the Old Jewish Cemetery and the surrounding synagogues. A combined ticket for all six Jewish monuments costs ~€15 and is well worth it for history lovers. Learn about the rich and tragic history of Prague's Jewish community.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the river and explore the Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods – two authentic, less-touristy districts beloved by locals. Visit the quirky Žižkov Television Tower (entry ~€8) for panoramic city views, and spot the famous crawling baby sculptures by artist David Černý on its exterior. Wander the leafy streets and browse local shops and markets.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert at one of Prague's many affordable historic venues – look for budget performances at the Municipal House (Obecní dům) or smaller churches (~€10–15 for standing/cheap seats). Alternatively, enjoy live jazz at a cozy basement bar in the Old Town. End with a late dinner at a Czech canteen (jídelna) for authentic and very cheap local food.

meals.breakfast: Sit-down breakfast at a local café with eggs, toast, and coffee (~€4–5)
meals.lunch: Svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce with dumplings) at a local Czech restaurant (~€6–8)
meals.dinner: Budget meal at a Czech canteen (jídelna) – soup, main course, and a drink (~€5–7)

day_by_day.notes: The Jewish Quarter can get crowded midday – visit early. Look for the David Černý 'Hanging Man' sculpture on Husova Street for a fun free photo stop. Check the Municipal House website for last-minute discounted concert tickets.

day_by_day.morning: Take a relaxing morning walk through Letná Park (Letenské sady) above the city for spectacular free panoramic views over Prague's red rooftops and the Vltava River. Locals jog and cycle here – it's a great way to experience everyday Prague life. Visit the giant metronome at the top of the hill, which stands where a Stalin statue once stood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Náplavka Farmers' Market along the riverside embankment (open Friday afternoons and weekends) – browse local produce, street food, artisan goods, and enjoy the vibrant atmosphere. This is a perfect spot to try affordable local Czech snacks and mingle with locals. Afterward, visit the free National Museum (Národní muzeum) exterior on Wenceslas Square (Václavské náměstí) and explore the bustling boulevard.
day_by_day.evening: Pack your bags and prepare for an early departure to Budapest the next morning. Enjoy a farewell Czech dinner at a traditional hospoda (pub) – try fried cheese (smažený sýr) or roast pork knee (vepřové koleno) with a cold Pilsner Urquell or Kozel beer. Book your overnight bus or early morning train to Budapest if not already arranged.

meals.breakfast: Grab-and-go breakfast from a supermarket (Albert or Billa) – yogurt, fruit, and a roll (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Street food at Náplavka Farmers' Market – try langos (fried dough with toppings) or grilled sausage (~€4–6)
meals.dinner: Farewell Czech dinner at a local hospoda – roast pork knee or fried cheese with fries and a beer (~€8–12)

day_by_day.notes: The Náplavka market is one of Prague's best local experiences and is completely free to browse. RegioJet and FlixBus offer affordable Prague–Budapest routes (from ~€15–25 if booked in advance). The journey takes approximately 7–8 hours by bus or 6–7 hours by train. Consider an overnight bus to save on accommodation.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive in Budapest by morning (if taking an overnight bus) or mid-morning (if taking an early train). Check in to your accommodation and freshen up. Begin exploring Budapest with a free self-guided walk across the iconic Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) connecting Buda and Pest sides of the city, with stunning views of the Danube River and Parliament building.
day_by_day.afternoon: Climb up Castle Hill (Várhegy) in Buda – explore the historic Buda Castle district, Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) with its fairy-tale turrets and free panoramic views, and the exterior of Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom). The views over the Danube and Pest from here are among the best in Central Europe. Take the historic funicular (~€4) or walk up for free.
day_by_day.evening: Cross back to the Pest side and explore the vibrant ruin bar scene in the Jewish Quarter. Visit Szimpla Kert – Budapest's most famous ruin bar – for affordable drinks in a quirky, art-filled courtyard setting. Grab street food from nearby vendors or eat at a nearby lángos (Hungarian fried dough) stand for a very cheap and delicious dinner.

meals.breakfast: On the bus/train or grab a fresh pastry and coffee at Budapest Keleti Station (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Lángos with sour cream and cheese from a street vendor near the castle (~€2–3)
meals.dinner: Budget Hungarian street food near the Jewish Quarter – chimney cake, lángos, or a quick goulash soup (~€5–7)

day_by_day.notes: Budapest is divided into Buda (hilly, historic) and Pest (flat, lively). Buy a Budapest public transport day pass (~€5) for unlimited tram, metro, and bus travel. The Fisherman's Bastion exterior is completely free – only the tower interior charges admission. September weather in Budapest is typically mild and pleasant (15–22°C).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the magnificent Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) – one of the largest parliament buildings in the world and an iconic Budapest landmark. Book a budget guided tour in advance (~€8–10 for non-EU citizens) or admire the exterior for free from Kossuth Square. Stroll along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) and enjoy views of the Buda Castle across the river.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Great Market Hall (Nagy Vásárcsarnok) – Budapest's largest and most beautiful indoor market. Browse stalls selling Hungarian paprika, salami, pickles, embroidery, and local produce. The ground floor is ideal for cheap lunch and grocery shopping. Afterward, walk along Váci Street (Budapest's famous pedestrian shopping street) and explore the vibrant Ferencváros neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to the quintessential Budapest experience – a soak at one of the city's famous thermal baths. The Széchenyi Thermal Bath is the most iconic (~€20–22 for evening entry, cheaper than daytime), while Rudas or Lukács baths offer more affordable and local alternatives (~€15–18). Relax in the warm mineral waters under the September sky. Grab a simple dinner afterward at a nearby Hungarian restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your accommodation or a local bakery – fresh bread roll with butter and coffee (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Hearty and cheap lunch at the Great Market Hall – try kürtőskalács (chimney cake), lángos, or a bowl of gulyás soup (~€4–6)
meals.dinner: Traditional Hungarian dinner near the thermal baths – chicken paprikash with egg noodles (nokedli) at a local étterem (~€8–10)

day_by_day.notes: Book thermal bath tickets online in advance to avoid queues and sometimes get small discounts. The Great Market Hall is closed on Sundays for regular shopping but the food stalls on the ground floor may still be open – check ahead. Sunday is a great day to visit Parliament Square as it's less crowded with weekday commuters.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) – one of Budapest's most iconic landmarks, featuring the Millennium Monument and statues of Hungary's greatest historical figures. Entry is completely free. Explore the surrounding City Park (Városliget) – stroll through the park, see the Vajdahunyad Castle (free exterior), and enjoy the peaceful green space in the heart of the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Jewish Quarter more deeply – visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (Dohány utcai zsinagóga), the largest synagogue in Europe (~€8 entry). Walk through the Memorial Garden and the Weeping Willow Holocaust Memorial. Explore the surrounding Seventh District (Erzsébetváros) with its eclectic architecture, street art, and vibrant café culture – a neighborhood full of history and energy.
day_by_day.evening: Take a free evening walk along the Danube Embankment to see the famous Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial – a moving tribute to Jews killed during WWII. Then enjoy the spectacular view of the illuminated Parliament Building and Chain Bridge at night – one of Europe's most beautiful cityscapes. End the evening at a local Hungarian wine bar for affordable local wines from the Tokaj or Eger regions.

meals.breakfast: Sit-down breakfast at a local café – scrambled eggs, bread, and coffee (~€4–5)
meals.lunch: Budget lunch at a Hungarian self-service canteen (étkezde) near the Jewish Quarter – two-course meal with soup and main (~€5–7)
meals.dinner: Light dinner with Hungarian wine at a local bor bár (wine bar) – cheese, charcuterie, and local wine (~€8–12)

day_by_day.notes: Heroes' Square and City Park are completely free to visit and are great for a relaxed morning. The Great Synagogue is one of the most historically significant sites in Budapest – allocate at least 1.5 hours. The Danube embankment is most beautiful after sunset when all the landmarks are lit up – perfect for a final evening stroll.

day_by_day.morning: Spend your final morning exploring the charming Buda neighborhoods of Óbuda (Old Buda) – the oldest part of Budapest with Roman ruins at Aquincum (~€5 entry) and a quiet, authentic village-like atmosphere far from the tourist crowds. Alternatively, visit the Budapest History Museum in Buda Castle for a deeper dive into the city's layered history (~€6).
day_by_day.afternoon: Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at the Great Market Hall or local shops – pick up Hungarian paprika, pálinka (fruit brandy), Tokaji wine, or embroidered goods as affordable gifts. Take a final walk across the Chain Bridge for one last panoramic view of this stunning city. Enjoy a leisurely farewell lunch at a traditional Hungarian restaurant.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Budapest airport (Liszt Ferenc International Airport) or your departure point. Take Bus 100E from Deák Ferenc Square to the airport (~€3, approximately 30–40 minutes). Reflect on an incredible 8-day journey through two of Central Europe's most beautiful and affordable capital cities.

meals.breakfast: Final Hungarian breakfast – fresh bread, cold cuts, cheese, and coffee at a local bakery (~€3–5)
meals.lunch: Farewell Hungarian feast – beef goulash or stuffed cabbage (töltött káposzta) at a traditional étterem (~€8–10)
meals.dinner: Grab-and-go food at the airport or a quick bite before departure (~€5–8)

day_by_day.notes: Budget approximately €15–25 total for souvenirs if desired. Bus 100E is the most affordable airport transfer – avoid taxis unless sharing. Overall trip budget estimate: accommodation €15–30/night per person in a hostel or budget hotel, daily food €15–25, transport and activities €10–20/day. Total estimated budget for 8 days: €350–500 per person including transport between cities.

trip_options.title: Classic Eastern Europe – Prague & Budapest Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Eastern Europe – Prague & Budapest

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled – in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Prague Václav Havel Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer to your accommodation via the Airport Express bus (Line AE) to Hlavní nádraží, then taxi or rideshare to hotel. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: If hungry upon arrival, grab a late-night bite at a 24-hour convenience store near the hotel or order room service. Alternatively, many Prague pubs serve food until midnight – try a nearby local hospoda (pub) for a quick svíčková (beef sirloin) or goulash.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – your priority is getting to the hotel safely. Pre-book your airport transfer if possible. Prague's public transport is reliable but stops running around midnight, so a taxi or rideshare (Bolt or Uber) is recommended for this late arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Start your Prague adventure with a leisurely breakfast, then head to the Old Town (Staré Město). Explore Old Town Square, admire the Gothic Týn Church, and watch the famous Astronomical Clock (Orloj) chime at the top of the hour. Climb the Old Town Hall Tower for panoramic views of the city rooftops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the iconic Charles Bridge (Karlův most), taking in the Baroque statues and views of the Vltava River. Continue uphill to Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) – explore St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane. The castle complex offers some of the best views of Prague's red-roofed skyline.
day_by_day.evening: Descend from the castle into the charming Malá Strana (Lesser Town) neighborhood. Stroll through cobblestone streets and enjoy the atmospheric evening lighting. End the day with dinner at a traditional Czech restaurant in the area.

meals.breakfast: Café Louvre or a nearby bakery – try a párek v rohlíku (Czech sausage in a roll) or fresh pastries with coffee
meals.lunch: Café Savoy in Malá Strana – mid-range Czech classics like svíčková or roast duck with dumplings (approx. €12–18 per person)
meals.dinner: U Malého Glena or Lokál Malá Strana – authentic Czech cuisine with local Pilsner Urquell on tap (approx. €15–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle is best visited on a weekday morning or afternoon to avoid weekend crowds. Wear comfortable walking shoes – the cobblestones and castle hill require solid footwear. Buy a combined castle ticket (approx. €14) for access to all major sites.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Josefov, Prague's historic Jewish Quarter. Explore the Jewish Museum complex, which includes six synagogues (Spanish, Pinkas, Maisel, Klaus, and Old-New Synagogue) and the hauntingly beautiful Old Jewish Cemetery. This is one of the most significant Jewish historical sites in Europe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Wenceslas Square (Václavské náměstí) in the New Town – a grand boulevard lined with shops, hotels, and cafés with deep historical significance (site of the 1968 Prague Spring and 1989 Velvet Revolution). Nearby, visit the National Museum (Národní muzeum) which houses impressive natural history and history collections. Walk through the Vinohrady neighborhood to see beautiful Art Nouveau architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a classical music concert – Prague is renowned for its live music scene, and evening chamber concerts are held regularly in historic venues like the Municipal House (Obecní dům) or St. Nicholas Church. Book tickets in advance online.

meals.breakfast: Café Imperial – a stunning Art Nouveau café offering hearty Czech breakfasts with eggs, cold cuts, and fresh bread (approx. €8–12)
meals.lunch: Kantýna – a modern Czech butcher-restaurant in the New Town serving excellent grilled meats and seasonal dishes at mid-range prices (approx. €10–15)
meals.dinner: Pre-concert light dinner at Café Restaurant Municipal House or a wine bar in Vinohrady – try Czech wine from Moravia with charcuterie boards (approx. €15–20)

day_by_day.notes: The Jewish Museum complex requires a separate ticket (approx. €16–20). The Old-New Synagogue has an additional entry fee. Photography is restricted in some areas. Book concert tickets at least 1–2 days in advance as popular venues sell out quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning day trip to Kutná Hora, a UNESCO World Heritage town just 1.5 hours from Prague by train. Visit the eerie and fascinating Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church), where the bones of approximately 40,000 people are arranged into chandeliers, coats of arms, and decorative elements. Then explore the stunning Gothic Cathedral of Saint Barbara.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Prague by mid-afternoon. Explore the vibrant Žižkov neighborhood – known for its quirky local character, the giant Žižkov Television Tower (with David Černý's crawling babies sculptures), and independent cafés. Visit the National Memorial on Vítkov Hill for sweeping city views.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Prague's famous nightlife scene with a progressive pub crawl through the Vinohrady or Žižkov neighborhoods – these areas offer authentic local bars away from the tourist-heavy Old Town. Try local craft beers from breweries like Matuška or Únětický pivovar.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at your hotel or a grab-and-go from a local pekárna (bakery) before catching the morning train
meals.lunch: In Kutná Hora – Dačický Restaurant, a charming medieval-themed eatery serving traditional Bohemian cuisine (approx. €10–15)
meals.dinner: Krásný Ztráty or a local Žižkov pub – hearty Czech pub food with craft beer (approx. €12–18)

day_by_day.notes: Trains to Kutná Hora depart from Praha Hlavní nádraží or Praha Masarykovo nádraží approximately every hour. Round-trip tickets cost approx. €10–14. The Ossuary is a 10-minute walk from Kutná Hora Sedlec station. Comfortable walking shoes are essential for the day trip.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take the morning train or bus from Prague to Budapest. The RegioJet train is a popular, comfortable mid-range option (approx. 6.5–7 hours, €25–45). Alternatively, FlixBus offers a budget option. Enjoy the scenic Central European countryside en route. Alternatively, a 1-hour flight is available for those preferring speed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest in the afternoon. Check in to your accommodation, then take a gentle orientation walk along the Danube riverbank. Stroll the Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) and take in your first views of Buda Castle Hill across the river. Get acquainted with the Pest side of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) if still open (closes around 17:00 on Saturdays), or browse the Ráday Street restaurant row for dinner options. Enjoy a relaxed first evening in Budapest soaking in the city's grand Austro-Hungarian architecture.

meals.breakfast: At your Prague hotel or packed snacks for the train journey
meals.lunch: On the train – bring packed food from a Prague deli or supermarket, or purchase snacks from the RegioJet dining car
meals.dinner: Borkonyha Winekitchen or Mák Bistro in central Budapest – contemporary Hungarian cuisine with excellent local wines (approx. €18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book your Prague–Budapest train or bus tickets in advance, especially for Saturday travel. RegioJet trains are highly recommended for comfort and value. Upon arrival, Budapest's BKK public transport (metro, trams, buses) is excellent – purchase a 24-hour or 72-hour travel card (approx. €5–10) for unlimited travel.

day_by_day.morning: Begin with Budapest's crown jewel – Buda Castle Hill. Take the historic Funicular (Budavári Sikló) from Clark Ádám Square up to the castle district. Explore Buda Castle and the Budapest History Museum, then walk through the beautifully preserved medieval streets to Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom) and the iconic Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) for breathtaking panoramic views of the Danube and Pest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross back to Pest via the Chain Bridge on foot. Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) – one of the largest parliament buildings in the world and a masterpiece of Neo-Gothic architecture. Book a guided interior tour in advance (approx. €10–15). Walk along the Danube Promenade and visit the moving Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Jewish Quarter (VII District) and explore the famous ruin bars (romkocsmák). Start with the legendary Szimpla Kert – Budapest's original ruin bar set in a crumbling courtyard filled with eclectic furniture, art, and live music. This is a uniquely Budapest experience.

meals.breakfast: New York Café – a breathtakingly ornate café often called 'the most beautiful café in the world'; try Hungarian breakfast pastries and coffee (approx. €10–15)
meals.lunch: Hungarikum Bisztró near the Parliament – traditional Hungarian dishes like gulyás (goulash), lángos, and stuffed peppers at mid-range prices (approx. €12–18)
meals.dinner: Szimpla Kert food stalls or nearby Kazinczy Street restaurants in the Jewish Quarter – diverse street food and local Hungarian bites (approx. €8–15)

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours must be booked in advance online. The Fisherman's Bastion is free to access the lower terraces; the upper terrace has a small fee. Sunday is a great day to visit as the Great Market Hall is closed but the city is lively with locals.

day_by_day.morning: Experience one of Budapest's most unique traditions – a morning soak at a historic thermal bath. Visit the magnificent Széchenyi Thermal Bath in City Park, a stunning Neo-Baroque complex with indoor and outdoor pools fed by natural hot springs. A 2–3 hour visit is ideal (entry approx. €20–25 including locker).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore City Park (Városliget) – stroll through the park, visit Vajdahunyad Castle (a fairytale-like complex built for the 1896 Millennium Exhibition), and see Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) with its impressive Millennium Monument. Walk down Andrássy Avenue – Budapest's grand boulevard lined with Neo-Renaissance mansions, a UNESCO World Heritage Site – toward the city center.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a performance at the Hungarian State Opera House (Magyar Állami Operaház) – one of the most beautiful opera houses in Europe. Even if opera isn't your passion, the building itself is extraordinary. Budget tickets start from €10–15. Alternatively, take a sunset Danube River cruise for stunning illuminated views of both banks.

meals.breakfast: Café Gerbeaud on Vörösmarty Square – Budapest's most famous historic café, serving traditional Hungarian cakes, strudels, and coffee (approx. €8–12)
meals.lunch: Gundel Restaurant near City Park – Budapest's most historic fine-dining restaurant with a mid-range lunch menu featuring Hungarian classics like Gundel pancakes (approx. €20–30)
meals.dinner: Pre-opera dinner at Klassz Wine Bar & Restaurant on Andrássy Avenue – excellent Hungarian wines and modern bistro food (approx. €18–25)

day_by_day.notes: Bring a swimsuit, towel, and flip-flops for the thermal bath (or rent towels on-site for a small fee). Book opera tickets well in advance – the Hungarian State Opera is world-class and sells out quickly. Danube evening cruises depart from Vigadó Square pier (approx. €15–25).

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest – visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (Dohány utcai zsinagóga), the largest synagogue in Europe and a stunning Moorish-Byzantine architectural masterpiece. The adjacent Hungarian Jewish Museum and the moving Tree of Life memorial in the courtyard are deeply poignant. Then browse the nearby Gozsdu Udvar courtyard for coffee and last-minute local shopping.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a final walk through the Central Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) for souvenir shopping – pick up Hungarian paprika, Tokaji wine, pálinka (fruit brandy), Herend porcelain, or embroidered folk textiles. Enjoy a last leisurely stroll along the Danube or through the Inner City (Belváros) before heading to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport for your departure flight. Allow at least 2–2.5 hours before departure for check-in and security. Reflect on an incredible 8-day journey through two of Central Europe's most magnificent cities.

meals.breakfast: Café Central – a grand historic café in the Inner City serving full Hungarian breakfasts with eggs, cold cuts, and freshly baked bread (approx. €8–12)
meals.lunch: Paprika – a classic Hungarian restaurant near the Great Synagogue serving farewell dishes of gulyás, chicken paprikash, and chimney cake (kürtőskalács) for dessert (approx. €12–18)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or a light meal before departure – Budapest Airport has several decent mid-range dining options in the departure hall

day_by_day.notes: The Great Synagogue entry is approx. €12–15. The BKK Airport Shuttle Bus (100E) runs directly from Deák Ferenc Square to the airport every 20–30 minutes (approx. €3). Alternatively, a taxi or Bolt rideshare takes 30–40 minutes depending on traffic. Leave ample time for the journey to the airport on your final day.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

meals.breakfast: On board / at departure airport
meals.lunch: On board / at departure airport
meals.dinner: Late-night room service or hotel bar – charcuterie board, Czech open-faced sandwiches (chlebíčky), and a glass of Moravian wine or Pilsner Urquell to toast your arrival

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is late at night. Keep Day 1 completely free of planned activities. Confirm private airport transfer in advance. Ensure hotel has late check-in arrangements confirmed. Prague's Old Town area is your base for Days 1–4.

day_by_day.date: 2027-09-16 (Wednesday) – Prague: Royal History & Old Town Magic
day_by_day.morning: After a leisurely breakfast, begin with a private guided walking tour of Prague's UNESCO-listed Old Town. Explore the iconic Old Town Square, marvel at the 15th-century Astronomical Clock (Orloj) as it chimes, and wander through the Gothic lanes of Josefov (the Jewish Quarter), visiting the Old Jewish Cemetery and Spanish Synagogue.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the legendary Charles Bridge on foot, taking in the Baroque statues and panoramic Vltava River views. Ascend to Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) – the largest ancient castle complex in the world. Tour St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and the Golden Lane with your private guide. Enjoy sweeping views over the red-roofed city below.
day_by_day.evening: Descend into Malá Strana (Lesser Town) for a sunset stroll through its cobblestone streets. Dine at a Michelin-recommended restaurant such as Field or Alcron for refined Czech-European cuisine with seasonal tasting menus.

meals.breakfast: Elegant hotel breakfast – freshly baked pastries, eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, fresh fruit, and premium Czech coffee
meals.lunch: Café Savoy (a beautifully restored neo-Renaissance café in Malá Strana) – traditional svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) or duck confit with red cabbage and bread dumplings
meals.dinner: Restaurant Field or Alcron – contemporary Czech tasting menu with wine pairing; expect dishes featuring Bohemian trout, venison, and seasonal foraged ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Book Prague Castle tickets and restaurant reservations in advance. Private guide recommended for the full day (approx. 6–7 hours). September weather in Prague is mild (15–20°C) – bring a light jacket for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the DOX Centre for Contemporary Art or the Mucha Museum dedicated to Art Nouveau master Alfons Mucha – a deeply cultural Prague experience. Spend a couple of hours absorbing the rich artistic heritage before heading to the Veletržní Palace (National Gallery) for an impressive collection of Czech and international modern art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the vibrant Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods – Prague's creative, less-touristy districts. Browse artisan boutiques, visit the iconic Žižkov Television Tower (with David Černý's crawling baby sculptures), and enjoy a private tasting session at a premium Czech wine or craft beer cellar.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a world-class performance at the stunning Prague State Opera or the National Theatre – book premium seats for an opera, ballet, or classical concert. Pre-theatre dinner at La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise, holder of a Michelin star, for an extraordinary multi-course Czech heritage cuisine experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – granola, seasonal fruit compote, freshly squeezed juices, avocado toast, and a barista-prepared flat white
meals.lunch: Eska – a celebrated Prague restaurant focusing on fermented, sourdough, and locally sourced ingredients; try their signature open-fire dishes
meals.dinner: La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise – Michelin-starred tasting menu (8–11 courses) inspired by 19th-century Czech cookbooks, with optional wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Opera and National Theatre tickets should be booked weeks in advance – opt for a box or premium orchestra seat. Smart-casual to formal attire required for the evening performance. The Žižkov Tower observation deck offers stunning city views at dusk.

day_by_day.date: 2027-09-18 (Friday) – Prague to Budapest: Scenic Transfer Day
day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely morning in Prague. Take a peaceful sunrise walk across Charles Bridge (far fewer crowds in the early hours) and stop for a premium coffee at a riverside café. Return to the hotel for a full breakfast and pack for the journey to Budapest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Prague by private luxury vehicle or opt for a first-class seat on the scenic EuroCity train (approximately 7 hours, passing through beautiful Central European countryside) or a short 1-hour flight. Arrive in Budapest by late afternoon. Check into your premium Budapest accommodation and freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Begin your Budapest introduction with a private sunset cruise on the Danube River – the most dramatic way to first see the illuminated Parliament Building, Buda Castle, and Chain Bridge. Disembark and enjoy dinner at Costes Restaurant (Budapest's first Michelin-starred restaurant) on the Pest side.

meals.breakfast: Final Prague hotel breakfast – full spread with pastries, eggs, cold cuts, cheeses, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: On the train or private vehicle – pre-arranged gourmet picnic box with artisan sandwiches, Czech cheeses, charcuterie, fruit, and sparkling water; or dine in the train's dining car
meals.dinner: Costes Restaurant, Budapest – contemporary European fine dining with Hungarian influences; seasonal tasting menu with sommelier-selected wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: If traveling by private car, consider a scenic stop in the Slovak countryside or the historic town of Bratislava for a brief 1–2 hour layover. First-class train (EuroCity) is a luxurious, scenic, and eco-friendly option. Confirm Budapest hotel late afternoon check-in. Danube cruise should be pre-booked as a private charter for the most exclusive experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take a private funicular (or chauffeured car) up Castle Hill to the Buda Castle District. Explore the Hungarian National Gallery inside the Royal Palace, the medieval Matthias Church with its stunning Zsolnay tile roof, and the Fisherman's Bastion for panoramic views over the Danube and Pest skyline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and cross the iconic Széchenyi Chain Bridge on foot. Explore the elegant Andrássy Avenue (Budapest's answer to the Champs-Élysées), a UNESCO World Heritage boulevard lined with neo-Renaissance mansions. Visit the Hungarian State Opera House for a guided interior tour of its breathtaking gilded halls. Browse the upscale boutiques of the Fashion Street area.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a performance at the Hungarian State Opera House if scheduling aligns (book premium seats in advance). Pre-show or post-show dinner at Onyx Restaurant (Michelin-starred) on Vörösmarty Square, offering refined Hungarian haute cuisine in a spectacular Art Deco setting.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – Hungarian specialties including lángos (fried dough), túrós táska (cottage cheese pastry), fresh paprika salad, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Rivalda Café & Restaurant inside the Castle District – elegant setting in a former convent courtyard; try Hungarian fish soup (halászlé) or chicken paprikash
meals.dinner: Onyx Restaurant – Michelin-starred Hungarian fine dining; tasting menu featuring foie gras, Mangalica pork, and Tokaji wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: September in Budapest is warm and pleasant (18–23°C) – ideal for walking. Fisherman's Bastion is particularly magical at golden hour. Book Opera House tickets and Onyx well in advance. The Andrássy Avenue area is walkable and very safe.

day_by_day.date: 2027-09-20 (Sunday) – Budapest: Thermal Baths, Markets & Jewish Heritage
day_by_day.morning: Begin with a luxurious private morning session at the legendary Széchenyi Thermal Baths or the equally grand Gellért Baths – Budapest's famous thermal spa experience in stunning neo-Baroque architecture. Book a private cabin and premium treatments (massage, mud wrap) for the full luxury experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) – Budapest's magnificent 19th-century iron market hall. Browse stalls of Hungarian paprika, Tokaji wines, handcrafted goods, and street food. Afterward, explore the historic Jewish Quarter: the magnificent Dohány Street Synagogue (the largest in Europe), the Jewish Museum, and the poignant Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Budapest's world-famous ruin bar culture – but elevated. Visit Szimpla Kert (the original ruin bar) for a curated cocktail, then move to a rooftop bar such as 360 Bar or High Note SkyBar for panoramic night views over the illuminated city. End the evening with a late dinner at Stand Restaurant (Michelin-starred) for contemporary Hungarian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Light hotel breakfast or in-spa refreshments – herbal teas, fresh fruit, yogurt, and pastries to prepare for the thermal bath experience
meals.lunch: Great Market Hall upper floor – authentic lángos with sour cream and cheese, stuffed cabbage rolls, kürtőskalács (chimney cake), and a glass of local Egri Bikavér (Bull's Blood) wine
meals.dinner: Stand Restaurant – Michelin-starred contemporary Hungarian cuisine; chef Tamás Széll's refined take on traditional Hungarian flavors with an exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book the thermal bath private cabin session in advance, especially for weekends. The Jewish Quarter is best explored on foot – allow 2–3 hours. Ruin bars are lively on Sunday evenings. Dress code at upscale bars and Stand Restaurant is smart casual.

day_by_day.date: 2027-09-21 (Monday) – Budapest: Danube Bend Day Trip & Fine Arts
day_by_day.morning: Embark on a private half-day excursion to the stunning Danube Bend (Dunakanyar) – one of Central Europe's most beautiful river landscapes. Visit the medieval hilltop town of Visegrád with its Royal Palace ruins and citadel offering sweeping views, then continue to the charming Baroque town of Szentendre, known for its Serbian Orthodox churches, art galleries, and craft shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Budapest by early afternoon. Visit the Museum of Fine Arts (Szépművészeti Múzeum) on Heroes' Square – housing one of Central Europe's finest collections of European masterworks including El Greco, Raphael, and Rembrandt. Stroll through the grand Millennium Monument and City Park (Városliget).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final grand Budapest evening with a private gourmet dinner cruise on the Danube – sailing past the illuminated Parliament, Chain Bridge, and Buda Castle while being served a multi-course Hungarian dinner with live classical or jazz music. A truly unforgettable finale to your Budapest stay.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast – eggs, fresh pastries, Hungarian cold cuts, Balaton cheese selection, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Szentendre – dine at Rab Ráby Restaurant, a charming historic restaurant in the heart of town; try Hungarian goulash soup, stuffed peppers, and homemade pálinka (fruit brandy)
meals.dinner: Private Danube dinner cruise – elegant multi-course Hungarian and European menu with wine pairing, live music, and unrivaled views of Budapest's illuminated UNESCO skyline

day_by_day.notes: Private car and guide for the Danube Bend excursion is strongly recommended over group tours. Szentendre is particularly charming and less crowded on weekday mornings. Pre-book the private dinner cruise well in advance as it is a popular premium experience. Heroes' Square and City Park are free to explore.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Take a last peaceful walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) on the Pest side, soaking in views of Buda Castle and the Chain Bridge in the morning light. Stop for a final Hungarian espresso or kávé at a riverside café. Pick up last-minute premium souvenirs – Tokaji Aszú wine, hand-painted Herend porcelain, or artisan Hungarian paprika from a specialty shop on Váci Street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel. Private luxury transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport or onward destination. Depart with extraordinary memories of Prague and Budapest.
day_by_day.evening: Departure / travel

meals.breakfast: Lavish final hotel breakfast – full spread with Hungarian and international options; treat yourself to a glass of Tokaji with fresh pastries as a farewell
meals.lunch: Airport lounge dining or a final quick bite at a premium café near the hotel before transfer
meals.dinner: On board departure flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international flight departure for airport transfer and check-in. Ask the hotel concierge to arrange premium gift wrapping for any fragile souvenirs like Herend porcelain. Consider joining airport lounge access (Priority Pass or airline lounge) for a comfortable pre-flight experience. This concludes your 8-day premium Prague & Budapest journey.
